name: l1_residency
supersedes: tools/microbench/crossings/protocol-v2.json cell l1_residency (version 2: knee table non-monotonic on both devices, not installed; report 'crossings（其余格）')
mechanism: memory.l1.residency l1.data_array_bytes, l1.reserved_bytes (engine cpp/core/memory_hierarchy.cpp l1_cap_lines: L1 data lines = (data_array - reserved - launch static shared - launch dynamic shared) / line_bytes)
why_v2_failed: v2 varied the launch's dynamic shared allocation S and assumed the L1 data budget shrinks by S. The knee table (h100-r2 / b300-r2, identical on both devices: S 0 / 32 / 64 / 96 / 128 / 160 / 192 KiB -> knee 184 / 16 / 48 / 48 / 112 / 80 / 48 KiB) is explained without any cache anomaly by the driver's default carveout choice: with no carveout hint the driver picks the smallest supported shared-memory configuration that holds the occupancy-maximising number of resident CTAs, each CTA needing S + 1 KiB (system reservation). A 32-thread CTA may be resident 32x per SM, so S = 0 -> 32 x (1 KiB + 8 B static) = 32 KiB + 256 B -> 64 KiB config -> L1 192 KiB (knee 184), S = 32 KiB -> 6 x 33 KiB -> 228 KiB config -> L1 28 KiB (knee 16), S = 64 -> 3 x 65 -> 196 -> L1 60 (knee 48), S = 96 -> 2 x 97 -> 196 -> 60 (48), S = 128 -> 1 x 129 -> 132 -> 124 (112), S = 160 -> 164 -> 92 (80), S = 192 -> 196 -> 60 (48). Supported configurations (CUDA programming guide, cc 9.0 and 10.x): 0, 8, 16, 32, 64, 100, 132, 164, 196, 228 KiB. The quantity the engine formula needs is therefore not a function of the launch's shared bytes alone; this hypothesis is tested by the diagnostic cells below and the leaf is measured with the carveout pinned.
probe: tools/microbench/crossings/l1_residency/probe/l1cap.cu version 3 (same chase kernel as v2: one CTA, lane 0 runs the dependent ld.global.ca.u32 chase over a footprint F of 128 B lines in random cyclic order, warm pass then timed pass, base pointer pinned in registers; the SASS gate of v2 unchanged). Host changes: (1) carveout cells: cudaFuncAttributePreferredSharedMemoryCarveout = ceil(100 * C / 228) for C in {0, 8, 16, 32, 64, 100, 132, 164, 196, 228} KiB, dynamic S = 0, block 32; (2) smem-vs-carveout cells: C = 228 KiB with S in {0, 64, 200} KiB and C = 100 KiB with S in {0, 64} KiB (one cell is shared with (1)); (3) default-hint diagnostic cells: carveout attribute left at the default (-1), S in {0, 32, 64, 128, 192} KiB x block in {32, 1024}; F sweep for every cell: 4 KiB to 256 KiB in 4 KiB steps; --launches 8 --reps 33; every cell records the requested carveout percent, S, block size and the launch's static shared bytes (cudaFuncGetAttributes sharedSizeBytes) in its params. The attribute calls are checked (MB_CHECK); a cell whose attribute call fails is recorded as failed, not silently rerun.

derivation.per_load: lat(cell, F) = median over launches x reps of (t1 - t0) / hops, hops = F / 128
derivation.hit_reference: hit(cell) = lat(cell, F = 4 KiB) (the 4 KiB chase is an L1 hit everywhere); the cell is valid only if hit(cell) is within 5 % of the smallest hit(cell) of the run (v2 saw 39.0 / 38.0 cycles per hop on h100 / b300 at every S; the memlat l1 leaf 52.5 / 38.47 is reported next to it, not used as a gate)
derivation.effective_capacity: E(cell) = the largest F such that lat(cell, F') <= 1.10 * hit(cell) for every F' <= F (first crossing; one step = 4 KiB)
derivation.carveout_cells: K(C) = E(C) + C for C >= 8 KiB; the C = 0 cell is reported only (a CTA always carries the 1 KiB system reservation plus the kernel's static shared bytes, so the driver cannot honour a 0 KiB configuration; its knee shows which configuration it did pick)
derivation.fit: OLS of E(C) on C over C >= 8 KiB: slope (expected -1) and intercept reported
derivation.install: data_array_bytes = round(mean over C >= 8 KiB of K(C)) to 1 KiB, reserved_bytes = 0 (the engine reads only the difference; no vendor array size is assumed); the residual 256 KiB - mean K, if positive, is reported as the unusable part of the array
derivation.smem_vs_carveout: E(C = 228, S) for S in {0, 64, 200} KiB and E(C = 100, S) for S in {0, 64} KiB reported side by side: equal E at equal C and different S means the L1 budget is set by the carveout configuration, not by the launch's shared bytes (engine finding, handed to the engine line; no cpp change in this protocol)
derivation.default_hint_diagnostic: for every default-hint cell the implied configuration is reported as config(E) = the supported configuration closest to 256 KiB - E - (256 KiB - mean K) and compared with the hypothesis config_hyp = smallest supported configuration >= n_max x (S + 1 KiB + static), n_max = min(32 CTAs per SM, 64 warps / warps per block) (cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor with the same attribute is also recorded for reference); agreement is reported per cell, not used for the install

acceptance.measured: every carveout cell C >= 8 KiB valid; max K - min K <= 4 KiB (one F step) over C >= 8 KiB; both runs give the same E(C) at every C >= 8 KiB; fit slope within [-1.10, -0.90]
acceptance.experimental: spread <= 8 KiB or one C differs by one step between runs, everything else as above: installed with evidence experimental and the K table in the source
acceptance.unrealised: otherwise: the K table is reported, the leaf is not changed

runs: two runs per device (run-a, run-b) in one job; identity.csv per run dir
install: memory.l1.residency root fields l1.data_array_bytes / l1.reserved_bytes on both devices (h100 replaces the hopper-prototype 262144 / 8192, b300 the structural placeholder 262144 / 0); source keys l1_residency.<device>.<run> with protocol tools/microbench/crossings/l1_residency/protocol-v3.json; the other residency fields (replacement_policy, sets, ways, resident_lines*) are untouched; one two-architecture 450 A/B round
not_allowed: no case-cycle tuning; no values from other machines; no threshold or derivation change after data; no install of a device whose SASS gate fails; no cpp change (the carveout rule is reported to the engine line)
